title: Proxy router
description: One local SOCKS5 port that picks a tunnel per destination. Rules are evaluated top to bottom and the first enabled match wins; anything unmatched takes the default action. Point tools at it with --socks5-hostname so the hostname reaches the rules.
setSystemProxy: Point the Windows system proxy here while running
bypassListLabel: Bypass list (semicolon-separated; these never reach the router)
pacDescription: Wired up with a PAC script, because Windows' plain socks= proxy setting means SOCKS4 and this listener speaks SOCKS5.
resolveForIpRules: Resolve hostnames locally so IP/CIDR rules can match them

ruleTable.empty: No rules yet. Without any, every connection takes the default action.

linuxProxy.title: Use the router for other apps
linuxProxy.sessionHeading: Every app started from your shell (add to ~/.profile or your shell rc):
linuxProxy.sessionNote: Takes effect after logging back in. Covers curl, git and most CLI tools, plus Chromium, Chrome and Electron apps outside GNOME/KDE. Apps that ignore all_proxy keep connecting directly.
linuxProxy.chromiumHeading: Or just Chromium / Chrome — add to the launch command or its .desktop file:
linuxProxy.firefoxSteps: Settings → Network Settings → Manual proxy configuration: SOCKS Host 127.0.0.1, port {{port}}, SOCKS v5, and tick Proxy DNS when using SOCKS v5.
linuxProxy.failClosed: Apps pointed here lose the network while the router is off — keep "Run the router" on, and enable start-with-system in Settings.
